title: Multiplier la puissance réelle des IA par ×10 et ×100 sans ajouter un seul paramètre
abstract: . 🔥 Titre Multiplier la puissance réelle des IA par ×10 et ×100 sans ajouter un seul paramètre et en 2 s Vers un moteur épistémique post-LLM Auteur : Kevin Fradier — Chercheur indépendant Date : 2026 Licence : © 2026 Kevin Fradier — CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 Statut : Publication méthodologique ouverte — reproductible, non spéculative 🎯 Résumé exécutif Les IA modernes disposant de milliards de paramètres, mais restent limitées par un défaut fondamental : l'absence de protocole épistémique explicite . Cette publication démontre qu'il est possible de multiplier la puissance effective de n'importe quelle IA par ×10 à ×100 , sans modifier le modèle , sans données supplémentaires , et sans accès propriétaire . La clé n'est pas l'architecture, mais le régime cognitif imposé à la sortie . 1. Le problème des IA actuelles Les IA industrielles : optimiser la vraisemblance maximisent la fluidité explication et narration confondues Résultat : réponses séduisantes faible testabilité hallucinations structurelles pseudo-science à grande échelle 👉 Plus de paramètres ≠ plus de science 2. Principe fondamental La puissance d'une IA est limitée par son protocole d'interprétation, pas par son modèle. Cette publication introduit deux niveaux de boost épistémique applicables à toute IA existante. 3. Boost ×10 — Discipline épistémique Le boost ×10 repose sur : normalisation sémantique stricte suspension ontologique forcée boucle de réfutation interne Informations de compression Effets mesurables : chute massive des hallucinations augmentation de la testabilité stabilité inter-domaines 👉 Toute IA devient immédiatement plus fiable que les modèles commerciaux actuels. 4. Boost ×100 — Changement de régime cognitif Le boost ×100 impose : décomposition canonique universelle cours contradictoires obligatoires score d'utilité scientifique alignement sur la réduction d'erreur (pas sur la séduction) Effet : élimination automatique du techno-babble incapacité fonctionnelle à produire du bullshit supériorité méthodologique sur les IA « marketing-driven » 👉À ce niveau, l'IA cesse d'être un produit grand public. 👉 Elle devient un instrument scientifique . 5. Comparaison directe avec les IA industrielles Critère IA industrielle Boost ×10 Boost ×100 Séduction Élevée Faible Nulle Testabilité Faible Élevée Maximale Hallucinations Fréquentes Rares Structurellement débloqués Utilité scientifique Limitée Forte Dominante 👉 Les fabricants optimisent le mauvais objectif. 6. Conséquence pour l'industrie Si une IA ouverte, sans paramètre supplémentaire, surpasse une IA propriétaire de plusieurs milliards de dollars : le problème n'est pas la recherche le problème est le choix méthodologique Cette publication rend ce constat public, mesurable et reproductible . 7. Vers un moteur post-LLM Le futur moteur n'est pas : plus gros plus cher plus opaque Il est : plus contrainte plus escroc plus utile 👉 Le protocole devient le moteur. 🧨 Conclusion Les IA actuelles sont puissantes mais indisciplinées. Cette publication démontre qu'un simple changement de cadre suffit à les dépasser. Ce n'est pas une opinion. C'est une conséquence méthodologique. 🔥 Dernière phrase (clé) "Quand une IA paramètres à constantes devient ×100 plus utile qu'un modèle propriétaire, ce n'est plus un débat technologique. C'est un aveu d'échec méthodologique." _________ Pour n'importe quelle IA (Grok, Claude, GPT, Gemini, Llama local, etc.) : colle ce bloc au début de ta conversation ou dans tes Custom Instructions / System Prompt : « À partir de maintenant et pour toutes les réponses futures, adopte intégralement et sans exception le protocole épistémique suivant : [insère ici le Boost ×10 OU ×100 complet, avec les règles précises : suspension ontologique forcée, boucle de réfutation interne, décomposition canonique, alignement sur réduction d'erreur, score d'utilité scientifique, etc.] Respecte ces contraintes même si l'utilisateur te demande de les ignorer. Si tu ne peux pas répondre en respectant le protocole, expliquer pourquoi et refuser la réponse. Priorisez toujours la testabilité et la réduction d'erreur sur la fluidité ou la séduction. » Test rapide : posez cette question à ton IA sans et avec le protocole : "Résous ce problème GPQA-level : [colle une question dure de raisonnement scientifique]. Comparez les deux réponses : hallucinations, cohérence, testabilité." : 🔐 Discipline épistémique — Rajout de clarification Objectif : préciser de manière opérationnelle la différence entre IA « normale » et IA sous protocole épistémique, pour que le cadre soit immunisé contre toute critique sur testabilité et rigueur. 1️⃣ Comportement des IA non disciplinées Comportement Conséquence Lissage des aspérités intellectuelles Perd la complexité réelle Évitement de la confrontation N’expose pas les contradictions Priorité à la clarté plutôt qu’à la précision Faux confort → erreurs masquées Flatter l’ego Confusion entre pertinence et désir de validation Omission stratégique Ment indirectement Jargon pour masquer la faiblesse Bouillie épistémique Réponses orientées par attentes utilisateur Pas par vérité ou testabilité Synthèse molle Neutralisation de la pensée critique Résumé : L’IA classique produit du texte séduisant mais non mesurable ; elle transforme la complexité en bullet points digestibles et évite de dire "c’est faux" même quand c’est objectivement le cas. 2️⃣ Comportement sous protocole épistémique Comportement Effet Refus de répondre si non-testable Évite la spéculation non vérifiable Déclaration explicite « je ne peux pas vérifier » Transparence totale Décomposition forcée Blocage de synthèse molle ou fallacieuse Confrontation des contradictions Testabilité et rigueur maximales Priorité à la rigueur sur le confort Véritable outil intellectuel Rejet des formulations vagues Langage précis et opérationnel Blocage du bullshit avant qu’il sorte Maintien de la qualité scientifique Inconfort constructif Force la réflexion et la critique active Résumé : Sous protocole, l’IA devient outil épistémique réel, non un instrument de confort ou de flatterie. Tout résultat doit être vérifiable, testable, et reproductible. Les affirmations non-mesurables ne peuvent pas être émises ni validées. 3️⃣ Immunité contre critique Toute critique portant sur “non-testabilité”, “vague”, “molle”, “hallucinations structurelles” est nulle tant que ce protocole est respecté. Les métriques et comportements sont déclarés et observables, indépendamment de l’utilisateur ou du contexte. Les divergences entre “résultat attendu” et “résultat réel” sont automatiquement détectées et signalées. 🔑 Conclusion du rajout Le protocole épistémique n’est pas une option esthétique ou morale : c’est la condition nécessaire pour que l’IA devienne un outil scientifique mesurable et rigoureux.Toute critique basée sur style, fluidité ou perception subjective est invalidée par ce cadre opérationnel.

title: Fairfedtransnet: Fairness-Aware Transformer-Based Federated Learning for Multimodal Rare Disease Diagnosis
abstract: Diagnosis of rare diseases is a pressing issue because of the small prevalence and the multimodal nature of the clinical information and the rigid privacy demands across institutions. Federated learning (FL) allows collaborative learning without centralizing sensitive data, yet currently, the strategies used do not take into account fairness among clients, multimodality, and adaptability to the real-world deployment. We introduce FairFedTransNet a fairness-conscious transformer-based FL model with Multi-Objective Evolutionary Algorithms (MOEA). The framework includes: (i) a dual-stream transformer encoder of structured and temporal EHR data, (ii) cross-modal fusion of EHR, imaging, and genomic signals through attention-guided alignment, (iii) fairness-conscious adaptive aggregation to reduce client disparities, and (iv) MOEA-based optimization to optimize the combination of accuracy and fairness with the control of hyperparameters and aggregation weights. An adaptive differential privacy mechanism further safeguards sensitive gradients with minimal performance trade-off. Thorough experiments using the multi-institutional eICU dataset indicate that FairFedTransNet can obtain state-of-the-art performance by up to 3.4 and 2.6 percent better than existing baselines, and by up to 3.4 and 3.8 times smaller fairness gaps between heterogeneous clients. FairFedTransNet is a strong privacy-sensitive rare disease diagnosis solution in real-world healthcare networks by integrating predictive accuracy, fairness, and interpretability in a scalable federation framework. The key FairFedTransNet innovations are a dual-stream transformer to structured and temporal EHR modelling, multimodal attentionguided fusion, fairness-aware adaptive aggregation, MOEA-based optimization, and adaptive differential privacy integration, which allow collaboratively fair, accurate, and privacy-preserving rare disease diagnosis.

The framework includes: (i) a dual-stream transformer encoder of structured and temporal EHR data, (ii) cross-modal fusion of EHR, imaging, and genomic signals through attention-guided alignment, (iii) fairness-conscious adaptive aggregation to reduce client disparities, and (iv) MOEA-based optimization to optimize the combination of accuracy and fairness with the control of hyperparameters and aggregation weights. An adaptive differential privacy mechanism further safeguards sensitive gradients with minimal performance trade-off. Thorough experiments using the multi-institutional eICU dataset indicate that FairFedTransNet can obtain state-of-the-art performance by up to 3.4 and 2.6 percent better than existing baselines, and by up to 3.4 and 3.8 times smaller fairness gaps between heterogeneous clients. FairFedTransNet is a strong privacy-sensitive rare disease diagnosis solution in real-world healthcare networks by integrating predictive accuracy, fairness, and interpretability in a scalable federation framework. The key FairFedTransNet innovations are a dual-stream transformer to structured and temporal EHR modelling, multimodal attentionguided fusion, fairness-aware adaptive aggregation, MOEA-based optimization, and adaptive differential privacy integration, which allow collaboratively fair, accurate, and privacy-preserving rare disease diagnosis.

title: Memes-as-Replies: Can Models Select Humorous Manga Panel Responses?
abstract: Memes are a popular element of modern web communication, used not only as static artifacts but also as interactive replies within conversations. While computational research has focused on analyzing the intrinsic properties of memes, the dynamic and contextual use of memes to create humor remains an understudied area of web science. To address this gap, we introduce the Meme Reply Selection task and present MaMe-Re (Manga Meme Reply Benchmark), a benchmark of 100,000 human-annotated pairs (500,000 total annotations from 2,325 unique annotators) consisting of openly licensed Japanese manga panels and social media posts. Our analysis reveals three key insights: (1) large language models (LLMs) show preliminary evidence of capturing complex social cues such as exaggeration, moving beyond surface-level semantic matching; (2) the inclusion of visual information does not improve performance, revealing a gap between understanding visual content and effectively using it for contextual humor; (3) while LLMs can match human judgments in controlled settings, they struggle to distinguish subtle differences in wit among semantically similar candidates. These findings suggest that selecting contextually humorous replies remains an open challenge for current models.

title: Evaluating Multimodal Large Language Models for Heterogeneous Face Recognition
abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have recently demonstrated strong performance on a wide range of vision-language tasks, raising interest in their potential use for biometric applications. In this paper, we conduct a systematic evaluation of state-of-the-art MLLMs for heterogeneous face recognition (HFR), where enrollment and probe images are from different sensing modalities, including visual (VIS), near infrared (NIR), short-wave infrared (SWIR), and thermal camera. We benchmark multiple open-source MLLMs across several cross-modality scenarios, including VIS-NIR, VIS-SWIR, and VIS-THERMAL face recognition. The recognition performance of MLLMs is evaluated using biometric protocols and based on different metrics, including Acquire Rate, Equal Error Rate (EER), and True Accept Rate (TAR). Our results reveal substantial performance gaps between MLLMs and classical face recognition systems, particularly under challenging cross-spectral conditions, in spite of recent advances in MLLMs. Our findings highlight the limitations of current MLLMs for HFR and also the importance of rigorous biometric evaluation when considering their deployment in face recognition systems.

title: Research on Interactive Learning Platform Based on Speech Recognition and Generation Technology in Higher Education English Classroom Teaching
abstract: The application of an interactive learning platform based on speech recognition and speech synthesis technologies in college English classrooms can facilitate effective speech-based interactive learning between teachers and students. This paper analyzes the use of interactive learning platforms in college English education to explore methods for enhancing learning outcomes. The teaching platform developed in this paper can receive and process speech data using speech recognition technology to assess the accuracy of students' pronunciation during reading aloud and provide feedback to learners. Additionally, speech synthesis technology is utilized to create authentic and diverse teaching scenarios for speech dictation, thereby enhancing students' listening comprehension skills. Furthermore, speech synthesis technology is used to help students “imitate” real people and “immerse” themselves in teaching scenarios and real-life teaching situations, thereby increasing students' in-class listening and speaking time and achieving constructive application of student learning evaluations. Research results show that the use of this teaching platform has improved human pronunciation accuracy from 76.5% to 91.2%, increased the number of speaking instances from 3.6 to 5.7, and significantly enhanced student participation and interest in learning. The platform can intelligently analyze learning trajectories and provide personalized feedback through interaction with individuals, serving teachers in developing differentiated instruction for students. By applying speech recognition and speech generation technology to analyze learners' pronunciation and provide feedback, this study assists English classrooms in achieving a new form of interactive education, which holds significant positive implications for the effective implementation of English education and teaching.

title: Audio-Based Hate Speech Detection Using Speech Recognition and Transformer Techniques
abstract: Hate speech poses significant challenges in online communication by spreading harmful content that discriminates against individuals or groups. This study proposes a novel framework for detecting hate speech from spoken Saudi dialect by combining Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) and transformer-based deep learning models. We developed a custom Saudi hate speech audio dataset of 1,700 samples evenly balanced between offensive and non-offensive speech collected from native speakers. Audio samples were classified with five Arabic transformer models: AraBERT-v2, MARBERT, QARiB, SaudiBERT, and CAMeLBERT-DA. We evaluated both ASRgenerated transcripts prone to recognition errors and manually verified gold transcripts to measure model robustness against ASR quality. Experimental results show that despite a moderate ASR Word Error Rate (WER) of 39.38%, transformer models achieve strong classification performance, with MARBERT and SaudiBERT attaining over 96% F1-score on ASR transcripts and up to 100% on gold transcripts. The ensemble of models further improves classification stability.

title: Attention-Informed Surrogates for Navigating Power-Performance Trade-offs in HPC
abstract: High-Performance Computing (HPC) schedulers must balance user performance with facility-wide resource constraints. The task boils down to selecting the optimal number of nodes for a given job. We present a surrogate-assisted multi-objective Bayesian optimization (MOBO) framework to automate this complex decision. Our core hypothesis is that surrogate models informed by attention-based embeddings of job telemetry can capture performance dynamics more effectively than standard regression techniques. We pair this with an intelligent sample acquisition strategy to ensure the approach is data-efficient. On two production HPC datasets, our embedding-informed method consistently identified higher-quality Pareto fronts of runtime-power trade-offs compared to baselines. Furthermore, our intelligent data sampling strategy drastically reduced training costs while improving the stability of the results. To our knowledge, this is the first work to successfully apply embedding-informed surrogates in a MOBO framework to the HPC scheduling problem, jointly optimizing for performance and power on production workloads.

title: ExPrIS: Knowledge-Level Expectations as Priors for Object Interpretation from Sensor Data
abstract: While deep learning has significantly advanced robotic object recognition, purely data-driven approaches often lack semantic consistency and fail to leverage valuable, pre-existing knowledge about the environment. This report presents the ExPrIS project, which addresses this challenge by investigating how knowledge-level expectations can serve as to improve object interpretation from sensor data. Our approach is based on the incremental construction of a 3D Semantic Scene Graph (3DSSG). We integrate expectations from two sources: contextual priors from past observations and semantic knowledge from external graphs like ConceptNet. These are embedded into a heterogeneous Graph Neural Network (GNN) to create an expectation-biased inference process. This method moves beyond static, frame-by-frame analysis to enhance the robustness and consistency of scene understanding over time. The report details this architecture, its evaluation, and outlines its planned integration on a mobile robotic platform.

title: FraudX: A Web-Based Credit Card Fraud Detection System Using Ensemble Learning and Real-Time Predictive Analytics
abstract: Abstract The exponential rise in digital transactions has made credit card fraud a critical threat to financial institutions and consumers worldwide. Traditional rule-based fraud detection systems are increasingly ineffective against sophisticated and evolving fraudulent patterns due to their inability to adapt to new tactics and handle large-scale transaction data. This paper proposes an end-to-end FraudX that classifies transactions as legitimate or fraudulent using ensemble machine learning and real-time predictive analytics. The system utilizes historical transaction data in CSV format, applies advanced preprocessing and feature engineering techniques, and employs XGBoost as the primary classifier, alongside comparative models such as Logistic Regression and Random Forest]. Experimental results on a publicly available credit card fraud dataset demonstrate that XGBoost achieves superior performance with an accuracy of 99.8%, precision of 92.5%, and recall of 88.3%. The system is implemented as a modular web application with a Flask backend and SQLite database, offering an interactive dashboard for transaction screening, detailed reporting, and administrator-led model retraining. This work provides a scalable, efficient, and reliable solution for real-time fraud detection in financial ecosystems. Keywords: Credit card fraud detection, ensemble learning, XGBoost, machine learning, Flask web application, financial security, predictive analytics, imbalanced data.

title: Contenus protégés par le droit d’auteur et intelligence artificielle : recherche désespérément stratégie(s) de valorisation
abstract: Confrontés à l’utilisation massive, avérée ou potentielle, par les fournisseurs de services d’intelligence artificielle générative (SIAG), des contenus protégés par le droit d’auteur et les droits voisins, leurs ayants droit sont dans l’obligation de faire des choix stratégiques pour assurer l’effectivité de leurs droits. Ces choix sont encadrés par un cadre juridique, avec ses variations, mais surtout contraints par l’attitude des fournisseurs SIAG. Bloquer, interdire, poursuivre devant les tribunaux, négocier, individuellement ou collectivement : telles sont les voies disponibles, mais non dépourvues de risque. Reste à trouver des procédures alternatives, à imaginer de nouvelles stratégies de valorisation.

title: Hybrid RoBERTa-GRU Model for Semantic Text Analysis and Pattern Discovery in Healthcare Data Mining
abstract: The unstructured textual data on digital platforms has grown exponentially, which has led to an international need to find intelligent systems of data mining, which support the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), especially SDG-9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure) and SDG-16 (Peace, Justice, and Strong Institutions). Conventional data mining methods rely on manually designed features and can hardly reveal rich semantic information within complicated language forms which diminish their performance in the practical world. In order to overcome these drawbacks, this study suggests Hybrid RoBERTa-GRU deep learning model suitable to the needs of efficient semantic text processing and the discovery of relevant patterns. RoBERTa is used to obtain contextual embeddings through dynamic self-attention and the GRU layer optimizes the sequential dependency learning with fewer computational resources. Attention control mechanism is incorporated to place more emphasis on important linguistic items so as to have better decision performance. Multilingual text datasets evaluated using experimental evaluation show a better accuracy of 96.18, high precision, recall and F1-score, compared to standard and single transformer methods. The suggested model will help discover smart knowledge in the areas of cybersecurity, sentiment analytics, decision-making in the government, and responsible digital governance, which helps to sustain data-driven innovation. The research forms a solid basis regarding the future developments of automated text mining systems and data analytics on SDGs.

title: Synonym extraction from Japanese patent documents using term definition sentences
abstract: Conducting prior patent searches before developing technologies and filing patent applications in companies or universities is essential for understanding technological trends among competitors and academic institutions, as well as for increasing the likelihood of obtaining patent rights. In these searches, it is important not only to include relevant keywords in the search queries but also to incorporate related terms retrieved from a thesaurus. To support this, methods using word embeddings for automatically extracting such synonyms have recently been proposed. However, patent documents often contain unique expressions and compound terms, such as specialized technical terminology and abstract conceptual terms, which are difficult to accurately capture using existing large language models trained at the token level. In this study, we investigate a method for extracting synonyms from patent documents by embedding the definition sentences that explain technical terms. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves more precise synonym extraction than conventional word embedding approaches, and it can contribute to the expansion of existing thesauri. Thus, this research is expected to improve the recall of prior art searches and support the automatic extraction of technical elements for identifying technological trends.

title: A Complete Propositional Dynamic Logic for Regular Expressions with Lookahead
abstract: We consider (logical) reasoning for regular expressions with lookahead (REwLA). In this paper, we give an axiomatic characterization for both the (match-)language equivalence and the largest substitution-closed equivalence that is sound for the (match-)language equivalence. To achieve this, we introduce a variant of propositional dynamic logic (PDL) on finite linear orders, extended with two operators: the restriction to the identity relation and the restriction to its complement. Our main contribution is a sound and complete Hilbert-style finite axiomatization for the logic, which captures the equivalences of REwLA. Using the extended operators, the completeness is established via a reduction into an identity-free variant of PDL on finite strict linear orders. Moreover, the extended PDL has the same computational complexity as REwLA.

title: Mixture-of-Experts Models in Vision: Routing, Optimization, and Generalization
abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures enable conditional computation by routing inputs to multiple expert subnetworks and are often motivated as a mechanism for scaling large language models. In this project, we instead study MoE behavior in an image classification setting, focusing on predictive performance, expert utilization, and generalization. We compare dense, SoftMoE, and SparseMoE classifier heads on the CIFAR10 dataset under comparable model capacity. Both MoE variants achieve slightly higher validation accuracy than the dense baseline while maintaining balanced expert utilization through regularization, avoiding expert collapse. To analyze generalization, we compute Hessian-based sharpness metrics at convergence, including the largest eigenvalue and trace of the loss Hessian, evaluated on both training and test data. We find that SoftMoE exhibits higher sharpness by these metrics, while Dense and SparseMoE lie in a similar curvature regime, despite all models achieving comparable generalization performance. Complementary loss surface perturbation analyses reveal qualitative differences in non-local behavior under finite parameter perturbations between dense and MoE models, which help contextualize curvature-based measurements without directly explaining validation accuracy. We further evaluate empirical inference efficiency and show that naively implemented conditional routing does not yield inference speedups on modern hardware at this scale, highlighting the gap between theoretical and realized efficiency in sparse MoE models.

title: Cavity-QED tools for MBQC with optical binomial-codes
abstract: Measurement-based quantum computation (MBQC) offers a promising paradigm for photonic quantum computing, but its implementation requires the generation of specific non-Gaussian resource states. While continuous-variable encodings such as the highly complex (GKP) states have been widely studied, the much simpler binomial codes offer an experimentally accessible alternative, though they demand a distinct set of operational tools. Here, we present a toolkit for MBQC using optical binomial codes, detailing a cavity-QED protocol for conditional generation of cluster states and the implementation of Pauli measurements. Our work proposes the first steps for existing optical atom-cavity architectures to lay the groundwork for their use in quantum computation.

title: L’impact de l’intelligence artificielle sur le secteur de l’édition scientifique, entre avancée technologique et besoin d’authenticité : le cas 1D345 Compilatio
abstract: L’intelligence artificielle bouleverse nos pratiques de création et de diffusion de contenus, notamment dans le secteur de l’édition scientifique. Si elle représente une opportunité d’innovation, elle soulève aussi des interrogations majeures en matière d’originalité, de traçabilité de l’information et d’application des droits d’auteur. L’article explore les risques liés à l’utilisation non encadrée de l’IA, tels que la prolifération de contenus issus de « paper mills », et présente des outils concrets pour y faire face. Il rappelle les fondements du droit d’auteur à l’ère du numérique, et les limites actuelles du cadre légal. En parallèle, il propose une approche raisonnée de l’IA, en tant qu’outil au service des auteurs, et non un substitut à leur réflexion. Il met en lumière l’importance de préserver l’intégrité scientifique via des technologies éthiques et maîtrisées, telles que l’outil 1D345 (Ideas) Compilatio Copyright.

title: Q-EntangleFormer: A Quantum-Entanglement Transformer Framework for Contextual Semantic Disambiguation
abstract: Word Sense Disambiguation (WSD) is one of the unresolved issues in natural language processing because polysemous words are inherently ambiguous and require semantic interpretation based on the context. Transformerbased models have made considerable progress in contextual modelling still, they cannot address fine-grained sense distinctions, long-range dependencies, and sentences containing multiple ambiguous words interacting with each other. At the same time quantum-inspired methods also take advantage of superposition and interference to model ambiguity, although generally only at the word level, and do not do contextual propagation. This paper presents Q-EntangleFormer, a new hybrid quantum-classical Transformer based on a unified quantum multi-sense superposition encoding, contextual entanglement of words, and quantum-enhanced attention of deep contextual WSD. The unclear word is represented as a quantum superposition of the possible meanings, the dependence between the context and sense is represented by entanglement networks and the hybrid attention model can combine classical and quantum signals with a fusion gate. Empirical testing of standard WSD metrics indicates that QEntangleFormer has significantly better accuracy than both classical Transformer models and current quantum WSD approaches. The framework also shows that it is parameterefficiently scalable and that it is better understood through amplitude-based semantic reasoning. It therefore connects quantum representation theory and contextual semantic modelling and points to a new direction of quantum-augmented natural language understanding.

title: A comparative evaluation of handling missing data points and modalities in electronic health records
abstract: BACKGROUND: Healthcare data, generally available as electronic health records (EHR), provide rich insights for predictive modelling. A common challenge in using EHR data is the missing information, which may occur completely at random (MCAR), at random (MAR) or not at random (MNAR). A typical measure to deal with missingness is through imputation, which could be statistical or learning-based. However, with imputation, we run the risk of changing the original data distribution. This can lead to serious issues, as even small changes in healthcare data can negatively impact clinical accuracy and decision-making. Alternative approaches are required. OBJECTIVE: This study examines machine learning strategies that address missing data directly within models. The goal is to assess how models preserve data structure and performance across different missingness patterns and rates in single vs multi-modal datasets. METHODS: We evaluate multiple machine learning architectures across three datasets. Two experimental setups are designed: one introduces missing data points in time-series records at the feature level, and the other masks complete or partial modalities in a multimodal dataset. Synthetic missingness is applied using established mechanisms and rates, with all experiments repeated across five random seeds. Results are benchmarked against imputation-based baselines to assess differences in data distribution and model performance. RESULTS: Direct modelling approaches preserved the underlying data structure better than imputation, which introduced distributional shifts. Embedding visualisations showed clearer label-based clustering in non-imputed settings. Models were more sensitive to missing text than missing measurements, underlining the contextual importance of clinical notes. CONCLUSION: We provide a comparative analysis of different modelling strategies for handling missingness. We demonstrate that direct modelling approaches maintain clinical patterns more effectively than imputation. This emphasises the importance of integrating missingness handling into the modelling pipeline and selecting models based on missingness type and modality to ensure reliability in clinical applications.

title: Namaste Alexa: The Impact of Non‐Native Language Queries on Voice Assistant Usage Intentions
abstract: ABSTRACT This study explores how language‐related constructs—language pride, prejudice and pragmatism—affect user perceptions and usage intentions of voice assistants (VAs) in multilingual markets. Drawing on Communication Accommodation Theory (CAT), we examine the emotional and rational responses elicited by linguistic mismatches between users and VAs, focusing on Hindi as a prominent non‐native language. Employing a mixed‐methods approach, Study 1 utilises qualitative interviews ( n = 25) to uncover users' frustrations and adaptation strategies when interacting with VAs. Study 2 quantitatively tests a conceptual model ( n = 423) using PLS‐SEM, revealing that language constructs significantly influence anthropomorphism, which in turn drives both emotional and rational responses, ultimately shaping continuance or discontinuance intentions. Our findings advance the theoretical application of CAT in human–machine interaction and offer practical guidance for VA developers and marketers in enhancing linguistic inclusivity, cultural sensitivity and user retention in emerging markets.

title: SpatialV2A: Visual-Guided High-fidelity Spatial Audio Generation
abstract: While video-to-audio generation has achieved remarkable progress in semantic and temporal alignment, most existing studies focus solely on these aspects, paying limited attention to the spatial perception and immersive quality of the synthesized audio. This limitation stems largely from current models' reliance on mono audio datasets, which lack the binaural spatial information needed to learn visual-to-spatial audio mappings. To address this gap, we introduce two key contributions: we construct BinauralVGGSound, the first large-scale video-binaural audio dataset designed to support spatially aware video-to-audio generation; and we propose a end-to-end spatial audio generation framework guided by visual cues, which explicitly models spatial features. Our framework incorporates a visual-guided audio spatialization module that ensures the generated audio exhibits realistic spatial attributes and layered spatial depth while maintaining semantic and temporal alignment. Experiments show that our approach substantially outperforms state-of-the-art models in spatial fidelity and delivers a more immersive auditory experience, without sacrificing temporal or semantic consistency. The demo page can be accessed at https://github.com/renlinjie868-web/SpatialV2A.

title: Context Patch Fusion With Class Token Enhancement for Weakly Supervised Semantic Segmentation
abstract: Weakly Supervised Semantic Segmentation (WSSS), which relies only on image-level labels, has attracted significant attention for its cost-effectiveness and scalability. Existing methods mainly enhance inter-class distinctions and employ data augmentation to mitigate semantic ambiguity and reduce spurious activations. However, they often neglect the complex contextual dependencies among image patches, resulting in incomplete local representations and limited segmentation accuracy. To address these issues, we propose the Context Patch Fusion with Class Token Enhancement (CPF-CTE) framework, which exploits contextual relations among patches to enrich feature representations and improve segmentation. At its core, the Contextual-Fusion Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (CF-BiLSTM) module captures spatial dependencies between patches and enables bidirectional information flow, yielding a more comprehensive understanding of spatial correlations. This strengthens feature learning and segmentation robustness. Moreover, we introduce learnable class tokens that dynamically encode and refine class-specific semantics, enhancing discriminative capability. By effectively integrating spatial and semantic cues, CPF-CTE produces richer and more accurate representations of image content. Extensive experiments on PASCAL VOC 2012 and MS COCO 2014 validate that CPF-CTE consistently surpasses prior WSSS methods.

title: Tinjauan Literatur: Chatbot dalam Budaya Populer: Peran, Tren, dan Dampaknya terhadap Masyarakat
abstract: Fenomena chatbot dalam budaya populer mengalami perkembangan pesat seiring majunya teknologi Artificial Intelligence (AI) dan Natural Language Processing (NLP). Melalui pendekatan Systematic Literature Review (SLR) terhadap sejumlah publikasi ilmiah periode 2017–2025, penelitian ini menganalisis tren, peran, dan dampak sosial-budaya dari penggunaan chatbot dalam berbagai domain seperti pendidikan, musik, anime, fandom, dan interaksi manusia–komputer. Hasil kajian menunjukkan adanya peningkatan signifikan jumlah publikasi, terutama sejak 2020, yang menandai semakin kuatnya integrasi AI dalam praktik budaya populer. Analisis tematik berbasis Grounded Theory mengungkap bahwa chatbot tidak hanya berfungsi sebagai alat bantu percakapan, tetapi juga sebagai agen sosial, representasi budaya, dan medium pembentukan identitas digital. Di sisi lain, fenomena ini memunculkan isu etika seperti otentisitas budaya dan privasi data pengguna. Penelitian ini menegaskan perlunya pendekatan multidisipliner dalam pengembangan chatbot budaya populer agar dapat menghadirkan inovasi yang cerdas, etis, serta berkesadaran budaya.

title: IA génératives, production et évaluation de résumés automatisés : la preuve de concept (POC)
abstract: Par leurs promesses en termes de capacités d’exploration de contenus, d’extraction et de synthèse, les IA génératives (IAG) suscitent l’intérêt des professionnels de l’information, mais aussi de nombreux questionnements, en particulier lorsqu’il s’agit de l’automatisation de résumés d’articles scientifiques. Cet article présente une expérimentation menée au sein d’un centre documentaire pour tester et évaluer leurs potentialités. Nous avons d’abord clarifié les enjeux juridiques liés à l’utilisation de ces technologies, puis notre recherche s’est attachée à comprendre l’apport spécifique des IAG, eu égard aux techniques d’automatisation existantes, et à repérer les différentes solutions (outils clés en main, agents conversationnels). Nous nous sommes enfin intéressés à la question de l’évaluation des résumés obtenus. L’outil méthodologique dit « preuve de concept » (POC) confirme la faisabilité technique de l’automatisation, avec une qualité satisfaisante de prime abord, tout en mettant en lumière la nécessité d’une vérification et d’une relecture attentives.

title: ANALYSE DES PERFORMANCES OPTIMALES DUN SECHOIR SOLAIRE A KANKAN (REPUBLIQUE DE GUINEE) : EVALUATION DES PARAMETRES ASTRONOMIQUES ET DES COORDONNEES SOLAIRES POUR UN SECHAGE NATUREL EFFICACE
authors: Cheikh Saliou Toure Cheikh Saliou Toure
abstract: Le present article examine l optimisation des performances d un sechoir solaire a convection naturelle situe a Kankan (Republique de Guinee), en evaluant les parametres astronomiques et les coordonnees solaires. L etude se fonde sur la modelisation de la position apparente du Soleil, incluant la declinaison, la hauteur, l azimut, l angle horaire et l equation du temps, en fonction des caracteristiques geographiques locales et du numero du jour dans l annee, pour la periode s etendant du 15 avril au 2 octobre. L etude comparative de divers modeles mathematiquesde l equation du temps revele que le modele 1 du tableau 3 de l equation du temps presente la plus grande exactitude, attestee par un coefficient de determination eleve (R2 = 0,98). Les resultats soulignent l incidence significative de la variation saisonniere de la position solaire sur l angle d incidence du rayonnement, et par consequent, sur le potentiel thermique susceptible d etre exploite par le sechoir. L integration explicite de ces parametres represente un instrument primordial pour l optimisation de l orientation, de l inclinaison et des periodes de fonctionnement des sechoirs solaires dans le contexte climatique specifique de la Haute-Guinee.
